#  Title:Multiresolution quantum field theory in light-front coordinates
Authors:[Mikhail Altaisky](https://arxiv.org/search/hep-th?searchtype=author&query=Altaisky,+M), [Natalia Kaputkina](https://arxiv.org/search/hep-th?searchtype=author&query=Kaputkina,+N), [Robin Raj](https://arxiv.org/search/hep-th?searchtype=author&query=Raj,+R)
View a PDF of the paper titled Multiresolution quantum field theory in light-front coordinates, by Mikhail Altaisky and 1 other authors
[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2106.15706) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2106.15706v3)
> Abstract:We analyse the use of wavelet transform in quantum field theory models written in light-front coordinates. In a recent paper [W.N Polyzou, Phys. Rev. D 101(2020) 096004] [this http URL](http://W.N.Polyzou) used x^+ variable as 'time', and applied wavelet transform to the 'spatial' coordinates only. This makes the theory asymmetric with respect to space and time coordinates. In present paper we generalise the concept of continuous causal path, which is the basis of path integration, to the sequences of causally ordered spacetime regions, and present evaluation rules for Feynman path integrals over such sequences in terms of wavelet transform. Both the path integrals and the wavelet transform in our model are symmetric with respect to the light-front variables (x^+,x^-). The definition of a spacetime event in our generalization is very much like the definition of event in probability theory.
